name: The Grey household at 2010 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_grey_w_l

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2010 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2010 Mr. & Mrs. W. L. Grey & dr..

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2010, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The four live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. Left off: Jessie Grey (one of two unmarried daughters in 1900; which one is the 1904 "Miss Grey" is not known, so both are named in that line's note); Walter Grey (a grown son the 1904 Blue Book does not list at the house); Florence Grey (one of two unmarried daughters in 1900; named in the note on "Miss Grey"). The 1910 census (T624 roll 241, ED 166 and 167) was read for this card's children: the children it lists, and those the Blue Book lists at the number from 1890 to 1911, are on the card with the years each lived here, whether or not they were at home in 1904. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: W. L. Grey
persons.printed_as: 2010 Mr. & Mrs. W. L. Grey & dr.
persons.note: The 1900 census lists Wm. L. Grey here as head, born January 1840, in Illinois, married thirty years, president of a tannery, owning the house free of mortgage (ED 40, sheet 9A, line 32, leaf n810); his father and mother are both written as born in Illinois. The Blue Book lists him at 2010 from its 1890 edition, among the members of the Calumet Club (1890, 1895) and the Union League Club (1890), and of the South Shore Country Club in 1908 and 1909. From the 1907 edition he is listed alone, and the 1910 census (ED 167, sheet 5B, line 71, leaf n1458) gives him as widowed, living on his own income, the house still owned free. That 1910 line also writes his birthplace as New York and his parents' as Germany, against the 1900 line's Illinois; several of its ages are left blank, which suggests someone other than the family answered, so the 1900 reading is kept.

born.note: The census gives January 1840, age 60 on 1 June 1900.

portrait_research.note: An individual portrait has not yet been verified in the period portrait books and Glessner House Museum article archive searched for this project. Any figure shown is a reconstruction, not an attested likeness.

occupation.note: Written as "Pres. Tannery" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900; the hand is hard to read and an earlier reading took it for a commission company, but the capital T and the letters of "Tannery" are plain at full size, and his son Walter's line below reads as work in the tannery office. Which tannery the census does not say, and no other source read names it.

persons.name: Mrs. W. L. Grey
persons.printed_as: 2010 Mr. & Mrs. W. L. Grey & dr.
persons.note: The 1900 census lists Sarah Grey here as wife, born February 1850, in Illinois, married thirty years, the mother of three children, all three living (ED 40, sheet 9A, line 33, leaf n810); her parents are both written as born in Illinois. The Blue Book prints "Mr. & Mrs. W. L. Grey" at 2010 through its 1905 edition (canvassed from September 1904) and William alone from the 1907 edition (canvassed from September 1906); the 1906 edition was not read. The 1910 census gives William as widowed. So she died between late 1904 and late 1906; no death notice has been read, and the date is inferred from the listings.

persons.name: Miss Grey
persons.printed_as: 2010 Mr. & Mrs. W. L. Grey & dr.
persons.note: The Blue Book prints '& dr.' after the household's name: an unmarried daughter at home, not named. 'Miss Grey' is the book's own form of address, not a recorded name. The 1900 census lists the unmarried daughters at home as Jessie Grey (born May 1875, in Illinois, single; ED 40, sheet 9A, line 34, leaf n810); Florence Grey (born December 1880, in Illinois, single; ED 40, sheet 9A, line 36, leaf n810). Which of them the 1904 line stands for, the book does not say.

persons.name: Walter C. Grey
persons.note: Listed at 2010 under his parents from 1891 to 1901 and again from 1909; the 1910 census lists him there as son. The 1902 to 1908 editions do not list him, so whether he lived here in 1904 is not documented. The 1900 census lists him at home as son, born June 1876, in Illinois, single, working in what reads as the tannery office (ED 40, sheet 9A, line 35, leaf n810).

persons.name: Elizabeth W. Grey
persons.note: The 1910 census lists her at 2010 as William L. Grey's daughter; her age reads 14, but the figures on that line are hard to read and the Blue Book prints her as 'Miss' from 1910, so she may be older. She may be the unnamed '& dr.' of the 1904 listing, or her sister Florence may; the book does not say. Sarah Grey told the 1900 census she had borne three children, Jessie, Walter and Florence, so a child born before 1900 who is not one of them cannot be hers; the 1910 line that calls this one William's child also gives the parents' birthplaces as New York, unlike the 1900 lines, so how they were related to William is not settled.

born.note: Re-reading the existing household note: the difficult 1910 age appears to be 14, implying about 1895-96. The reading may be wrong and is retained as uncertain; the Miss title is not enough to assume an adult in 1904.

persons.name: Florence Grey
persons.note: Listed at 2010 with William L. Grey in the 1907 and 1908 editions. That she was a daughter of the house is read from the shared surname and 'Miss' at the number; the Blue Book does not print the relationship. The household printed '& drs.' from 1895 to 1902 and '& dr.' from 1903 to 1906, so she may be the daughter at home in 1904.
